## Simple shear {-}

### Simple shear in 2D {-}
The reference body $B_{\rm{Ref}}$ is a subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$. The deformation map, $\bsf{x}\ag{\cdot}$, takes points from $B_{\rm{Ref}}$ into $\mathbb{R}^2$. We will denote the set $\bsf{x}\ag{B_{\rm{Ref}}}$ as $B_{\tau}$, the deformed body.

We can talk about the deformation map $\bsf{x}\ag{\cdot}: B_{\rm Ref}\to \mathbb{R}^2$. 

$$
\begin{align}
x_1[X_1,X_2,X_3]&=X_1+0.2 t X_2,\\
x_2[X_1,X_2,X_3]&=X_2,\\
\end{align}
$$

### Simple shear in 3D {-}


$$
\begin{align}
x_1[X_1,X_2,X_3]&=X_1+0.2 t X_2,\\
x_2[X_1,X_2,X_3]&=X_2,\\
x_3[X_1,X_2,X_3]&=X_3,\\
\end{align}
$$

The above defomation map can also be written as

$$
\begin{align}
x_1[X_i]&=X_1+0.4 X_2,\\
x_2[X_i]&=X_2,\\
x_3[X_i]&=X_3,\\
\end{align}
$$


Since 
$$
\begin{align}
x_1[\bsf{X}]&=\bsf{X}_{\cdot 1}+0.4  \bsf{X}_{\cdot 2},\\
x_2[\bsf{X}]&=\bsf{X}_{\cdot 2},\\
x_3[\bsf{X}]&=\bsf{X}_{\cdot 3},\\
\end{align}
$$

$$
\begin{align}
\bsf{x}\ag{\bsf{X}}&=\bsf{F} \bsf{X}
\end{align}
$$

where 
$$
\begin{align}
\bsf{F}_{\tau}
=\begin{bmatrix}
1 & 0.4 & 0\\
0 & 1 & 0\\
0 & 0 & 1
\end{bmatrix}
\end{align}
$$
